fix: Stop returning a freshly collected Vec from `accept` (and `cancel`/`entries` if they are on the same path). Either fill a caller-owned buffer, `pub fn accept(&mut self, key: GestureArenaKey, member: GestureArenaMember, out: &mut Vec<GestureArenaEntry>)` with `out.clear()` then `out.extend(...)`, so the caller reuses one buffer, or return `impl Iterator<Item = GestureArenaEntry> + '_` built from `entries.iter()`. Callers must be updated and the CHANGELOG noted if the signature changes.

`accept` builds the same snapshot `Vec<GestureArenaEntry>` in two places (here and at the end, lines 130-136). Extract one private helper, e.g. `fn snapshot(entries: &[(GestureArenaMember, bool, GestureDisposition)]) -> impl Iterator<Item = GestureArenaEntry> + '_` (or a fn returning the Vec), and call it from both return sites.

Replace the anonymous tuple with a named struct so the `.0`/`.1`/`.2` accesses at lines 104, 116-125, 133-135, 150 read by name: `struct StreamEntry { member: GestureArenaMember, simultaneous: bool, disposition: GestureDisposition }` and store `Vec<StreamEntry>`.

`mem::take` leaves an empty `Vec` with no capacity in the shared cell, so the next resolution's push allocates again. Keep a spare buffer: add a `spare: Vec<(u64, GestureDisposition)>` field to `ArenaGestureRecognizer`, then in `decide` do `let spare = std::mem::take(&mut self.spare); let mut requests = std::mem::replace(&mut *self.requests.borrow_mut(), spare);`, iterate `requests.drain(..)`, and restore with `requests.clear(); self.spare = requests;` on every return path (including the early `return GestureDecision::Reject`). The sink's Vec then keeps its capacity across resolutions.
